name: Scotch Gambit
family: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4 Scotch Gambit (Haxo, Advance, Max Lange, Anderssen)
summary: The Scotch Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4) gives up the d4 pawn for rapid development and pressure on f7. Against the main 4...Bc5 5.c3 Black can keep the pawn only by giving it back, and the d-file and the bishop pair open a level, open game. Against 4...Nf6 White chooses between the Advance (5.e5), the Max Lange attack (5.O-O Bc5) and the Anderssen double-gambit line, and the file covers traps such as 5...dxc3 Bxf7+ and the quiet transpositions to the Italian Game.
keyIdeas: Give up the d4 pawn for fast development and an open centre, aiming Bc4 at the f7 weak point.
After 4...Bc5 5.c3 the d4 pawn is regained by cxd4, reaching a level, open game with a big centre.
In 5...dxc3 lines Bxf7+ and Qd5+ punish greedy pawn-grabbing; keep the king-side tactics in mind.
Against 4...Nf6 choose the plan: the Advance 5.e5, the Max Lange 5.O-O Bc5 6.e5, or the Anderssen 5.O-O Nxe4 6.Re1.
The Max Lange attack uses e5, the Re1 check and Ng5 to hit Black's centre and f7.
Take care with the e4 pawn: ...Nxe4 is usually answered by Re1 pressure rather than an immediate knight grab.
Quiet 3rd-move answers (3...d6, 3...Nxd4) transpose to known Italian structures or lose a tempo to dxe5.
typicalPlans: Recapture on d4 with the c-pawn, castle, and use the open d- and e-files.
Pressure b7 and f7 with Qb3 and the Bc4 while keeping the centre pawns together.
commonMistakes: Grabbing e4 with the knight without checking Re1 and Bxf7+ ideas (Max Lange style).
Retreating the Bc4 to a3 after ...d5 (10.Ba3?) so the bishop is lost to ...dxc4; retreat to d3 instead.
Forgetting that the d-file is closed by the d4 pawn, so Qd5+ tactics only appear after ...dxc3.

lines.name: Haxo: 5.c3 Nf6 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Bd2 (main)
lines.description: Black's most solid answer to 5.c3 is 5...Nf6, and 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Bd2 trades the bishops while the centre opens. Black plays ...d5 to hit the Bc4 and open the d-file, and 10.Qb3 keeps White's initiative against b7. The less common 5...Bb6 retreat (about 0.4 behind) is met by 6.cxd4, keeping the centre.
lines.evaluation: Roughly level (about 0.00 to +0.1 through 10.Qb3); White keeps a stable centre.
